messages:
Ava: Quick sync—bench narrative for launch. Need final chart set + copy for blog + 2 webinar hooks. Who can own visuals?
Ravi: I can take visuals. Thinking 3 charts: latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), unit cost over tokens, and a heatmap of throughput vs instance type. Prefer clean axis labels: `x: input length`, `y: 99p latency (ms)`.
Sam: +1 on axes. For the blog blurb we should frame as "What real customers pay for predictable latency" rather than raw lowest latency.
Elena: Agree. Messaging: highlight predictable SLO + unit-econ gains from batching/caching. Two taglines: "Fast when you need it, cheaper when you don't" and "Predictable performance, predictable costs".
Ava: Nice. Ravi, can you mock the three charts by EOD? Sam, draft 2 short-post variants for Twitter/LinkedIn — one technical, one customer-impact. Elena, draft webinar title + 3 bullets.
Ravi: Will do. Quick Q on chart types — prefer line or area for unit cost?
Elena: Line for unit cost makes comparisons clearer. Area for latency distribution to show tails.
Sam: Draft posts will include CTAs: 1) "See benchmarks" 2) "Register for webinar". We'll A/B test CTAs and hero stat (latency vs $/1k tokens).
Ava: For webinar, schedule at 10am PT Thurs. Target audience = infra/platform + ML engs. CTA on registration form should route leads: Tier 1 (enterprise interest) -> AE queue; Tier 2 (self-serve) -> nurture flow.
BenchBot: Note: Marketing form integration requires mapping `lead_source=benchmark-2026` and `priority` rules. I'll post the payload snippet.
BenchBot: ```json
{"lead_source":"benchmark-2026","priority":"auto"}
```
Ravi: Chart note — include sample annotation on the latency chart showing canary rollback threshold and cost saving callout.
Elena: Also prep 3 short case-play scripts for webinar demo: 1) low-latency chat 2) high-throughput embeddings 3) cost-savings on batch inferencing.
Sam: I'll add short headlines for each: "Chat—sub-100ms real-time" , "Embeddings—scale 10x" , "Batch—40% token-cost reduction".
Ava: Perfect. Let's reconvene tomorrow morning 9am PT to review mocks and copy. Thanks all :thumbsup:
